_comment: What this pack measured when it was last validated.
It is a record, not an input: the gates live in profile.json and are checked
by scripts/validate-pack.mjs. This is here so a later run can see whether a
number moved, and by how much, rather than only whether it still clears a
profileFoldDigest: see validate-pack output; changing it invalidates the built index

_note: Six of these numbers were already stale when the 2026-08-05 rebuild
remeasured them — median 1773 -> 1803, p90 6008 -> 6010, max 17786 ->
17790, rowShapedLines 1911 -> 1921, tableRowsRecovered 2103 -> 2098,
romanPoints 10 -> 9. Nothing in that rebuild touches the grammar, and
content/ and the built bundle report the same figures, so this is the
record catching up with a parse it had already been given.
The parser moved from Gutenberg's plain text to its HTML on 2026-07-30.
Every number here moved with it, and none of the movements is a loss:
topics 135 -> 114. The plain-text parser opened a topic wherever it took a
paradigm caption for a run-heading, so amō and amor were two topics and the
six irregular verbs were six. The HTML has real headings, so those runs sit
under the heading the book gave them. No section became unreachable —
`assigned` went up, not down.
sourceSections 371 -> 376. The old reader required section numbers to run
strictly +1 and lost §372-375 (prosody, dropped either way) plus §222A.
textChars are measured on the words: the inline emphasis markup is stripped
before counting (see core's plainText). The median rose because whole
table cells now arrive whole, where the plain text truncated them at the
column edge and left the remainder as a loose line.
rowShapedLines 2015 -> 1911 with tableRowsRecovered 2052 -> 2103: fewer
lines carrying more rows, which is the wrapped-cell bug being fixed. A
cell that used to wrap over three physical lines is now one row.

_comment: The pack's further grammars, one entry apiece. Bennett is above, because
he is the syllabus the app teaches; these are gated to the same standard
and read by nothing at runtime yet.

lane.book: Lane, A Latin Grammar for Schools and Colleges (1898)

_note: What the crosswalk carries, not what Lane was written for: Lane's
topics are served out of the questions written against Bennett, so
a Lane topic no table row reaches has nothing to teach from.
The 224 unreached are 148 inflection topics and 76 others, because
lane-topics.tsv was built for the quotation pipeline and covers
§1056-2421 — Part Second — and nothing else. Extending it over
§§397-1022 is a model run nobody has paid for yet.
First measured 2026-08-11, the commit that wrote lane-parse.py.
Only maxTopics needed a threshold of its own (300-600, against Bennett's
60-300). Every other gate Bennett was calibrated at, Lane clears
unchanged — which is the finding, not a coincidence: the two books
disagree about how many topics a grammar has, and agree about how long
one should be.
The 714 dropped are §§1-396 (sound and word formation) and §§2428-2745
(prosody and versification), the ranges answering to the Parts Bennett's
own parser drops. G9 has not been read through.

_quotedNote: 2,387 of these questions have an answer somebody wrote, over 62 topics,
out of three pools that are not alternatives — 889 over 50 topics before
the 2026-08-11 Lane run. 308 came from the dictionary dump through
build-quote-pool.mjs; 581 from Allen & Greenough through ag-quotes.mjs;
and 1,498 from this run through lane-quotes.mjs, which reads Lane's Latin
Grammar (Project Gutenberg #44653). Like A&G it needs neither dump nor
dictionary, because it prints the sentence already macronized, credits it,
and translates it.
The 1,498 are NOT all Lane's. quote-tests pools all three files before
applying the minQuestionsPerTest floor, so stranded A&G and dump sentences
— ones that had never shipped, and so never collided with a prompt — went
in wherever Lane pushed their topic past three. Nothing on a shipped
question records which pool it came from, so the delta is one compose run
over three pools and not attributable to Lane alone.
Attested share by family, and what it says: verb-syntax 44%, noun-syntax
37%, adj-pron-syntax 35%, style 18%, particles 13%, then pron, verb-forms,
adj and nouns at 1-2%. The four inflection families did not move and were
never going to; REVIEW.md predicted exactly that and the run confirmed it.
C3 was the only gate that failed, and it failed on arithmetic rather than
on content: 1,498 questions raised the pack mean from 65.5 to 78.7 q/topic,
which lifted the 0.5x floor past `pron` sitting unchanged at 38.8. Nobody
quotes Cicero to teach the declension of hic, so that family can only grow
by generation, and it was topped up with 4 generated tests over bn-086 and
bn-088 — 16 questions, kept 100%, and E2 did not move. The alternative was
dropping about 122 attested sentences to satisfy a ratio.
dictResolvedPct 99.4 -> 99.1, on answerTokens 53,214 -> 65,132. The
attestation budget did NOT move with it: E2 is 105 unattested tokens and
89 distinct forms, the same figures as before, and E1's worst question
still carries 2. That is the invariant that matters here, and it holds
because quote-tests ships a quotation only when it carries no unattested
form at all. Why C5's percentage slipped three tenths on a pack whose
hard-miss count is unchanged has not been run down, and is recorded as an
open question rather than explained away.
A&G's half is filed by SECTION, not by sentence, and the map it uses is
committed at grammar/ag-topics.tsv — 147 rows a reviewer can read. Filing
sentence by sentence was tried first and abandoned: a model shown a bare
sentence has only its surface, and `Quid ipse sentiam expōnam` looks like
`Exspectās fortasse dum dīcat`, so the sentences of 64 of 147 A&G sections
scattered across two Bennett topics or more, up to seven. Asking once per
section, with A&G's own prose attached, brought that to 6 of 147 and cost
6 model calls rather than 24.
This was the first time quote-tests.mjs ran twice against one pack, and
it is what turned up three things latent since Greek ran it once. The
-q<n> counter restarted from 1 and would have written a second -q1 into a
file that already had one, which no gate checks — C0 checks test files
name a real topic, G5 checks duplicate topic ids, neither checks a test
id. quote-stats.json was a single object, so the second run erased the
first run's funnel. And --from fell through to Greek's path on a typo,
reporting a clean empty funnel. All three are fixed; ids are seeded from
what is already in the file, the stats are an array of runs.
_note: Three backfill runs took the syllabus from 1,088 tests to 1,722, and every
topic is at or above its size-scaled target. The gap the coverage report
was built to expose is closed.
The 2026-07-30 reparse regrouped the syllabus, so 27 topics' tests were
carried onto the topic that now covers their sections (see
scripts/remap-tests.mjs). Nothing was regenerated and nothing was thrown
away — hence max 26 -> 63 tests on a topic, which is six merged paradigm
topics' worth of drills under one heading. Only §313, which the old
parser had swallowed into Conditional Sentences, was newly generated.
keptRatioPct covers two of the three backfill runs. gen-stats.json is
written when a run finishes, and the middle run was stopped by hand before
it wrote anything, so roughly 270 shipped tests have no rejection-rate
data. C6 reads green on what it can see, not on everything.

_formKeysNote: 893,854 -> 973,267 when build-lemmas started attaching a wordform
entry's forms to the ranked lemma it says it is a form of. Wiktionary
gives a Latin participle its own entry and its own declension and leaves
the parent verb listing the citation form alone, so capiō — rank 245 —
shipped without captūrōs or any other form of its own future participle.
Note that no lemma was added: 55,312 before and after. The forms were
always the forms of a word the corpus counted; nothing could find them.
The count only moved once --max-rank 20000 was passed. The script's
default of 7000 does not reproduce what this pack ships and rebuilding
at it silently drops ranks 7001-19342 — 712 answer tokens' worth of
_note: Rebuilt on 2026-08-06, and this is the first record of a pack that ships
the whole dictionary rather than a corpus's vocabulary.
The word that caused it was `reste`. It is the ablative of `restis`,
rope; Wiktionary has it; the app said it was not in the dictionary. The
cause was never a rank cutoff — --max-rank was already past the end of
the list — but the list itself: build-lemmas walked ranked lemmas only,
and Latin's frequency list is seven works long. Apicius, Augustine,
Caesar, Catullus, Cicero, Ovid and Seneca between them never needed a
rope, so `restis` had no rank and was never visited.
distinctLemmas 19,292 -> 55,312, formKeys 491,398 -> 893,854. The tail
is every lemma entry the dictionary holds that the ranked half missed:
36,021 of them, unranked on purpose. Of the reference's 885,996 entries
only 52,424 are lemmas at all — the other 833,572 are wordform entries
(`amābam` as its own row), already reachable through the forms table of
the entry they point at, and shipping them would have multiplied the
file to add nothing.
The two mean-gloss figures are the point of the split. A ranked word is
one the student will meet again and gets six senses; a tail word is one
they are checking once and gets two, capped at 140 characters. Six for
everything would have cost about 2 MB on a phone to say more about
words nobody is learning.
nounGenderPct 99.2 -> 98.7 and meanGlossChars 72 -> 47 are both the tail
arriving, not a regression: the ranked half still reads 59 characters a
gloss, and the tail is thinner because it was written to be.
packResolvedPct is unchanged at 99.3 by construction. `attests` now asks
for a *ranked* record rather than merely a key, so C5 and gen-tests's
ok/unverified classifier are exactly as strict as they were when the map
held ranked lemmas alone. Shipping the tail widens what a student can
look up and nothing else.
305 -> 105 unattested tokens: 38 the enclitic on marīque and trēsve, 23
mid-sentence proper nouns the checker now exempts as the generator
always did, and 139 from build-lemmas learning to attach a participle's
declension to its parent verb.
What is left is not invented Latin. It is archaic gerundives (capiundae,
potiundī), -ier passive infinitives (aperīrier, mūnīrier), -ībam
imperfects (audībam, nescībam), regular comparatives no dictionary
enumerates, and sentence-initial proper nouns. Every one of the archaisms
sits in bn-116 peculiarities-of-conjugation or bn-338 the-gerund — the
topics that exist to teach exactly that form. Regenerating them would
make E2 greener and the pack less true, so the budget records them
instead. It is 105, and it has no headroom on purpose: the next run that
writes a form the reference cannot confirm has to raise it deliberately
and say which questions bought the increase.
71 more tokens are in reference/dictionary.db and not in what the pack
ships. They are a thin index rather than a bad sentence; closing that gap
is a build-lemmas job and touches no question.
The dictionary went from 2.1 MB to 4.2 MB across its two files when the
tail went in. Neither is precached, so what the study loop costs on a
plane is unchanged at ~427 KB; what moved is the one-time fetch the
vocabulary feature makes, and the screens that warn about it now read
their figure from the built files rather than from a number typed by
hand (see __DICTIONARY_BYTES__).
content/ is written in the same split shape the bundle is — a lemma
table plus a sorted form index — so build-web-content copies it through
rather than splitting it. The old denormalized map repeated a gloss
under every form and inflated to 116 MB for a third of these words; at
this size it would have been some 300 MB, which is more than apps/cli
could parse.
